speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if you have experienced any fever or fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the blisters on your forearm and pain with eating (suggesting oral ulcers), along with your recent use of captopril, are the forearm lesions itchy or painful, and do they have a central clearing or target-like appearance? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Renal_Function_Panel. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Status, ANA, Anti-SSA, Anti-SSB, Anti-dsDNA.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN)
The combination of recent captopril initiation, the specific history of pain with eating and sexual intercourse (mucosal involvement), and the forearm blisters is highly suggestive of SJS/TEN, a severe hypersensitivity reaction. Since the CBC and metabolic panels are normal and we have ruled out immediate infectious causes, this clinical picture fits the drug-induced etiology.
